title: Modified Premium Calculator
description: Workers'-compensation modified premium: subject premium (total manual premium plus premium items subject to experience rating) times the experience modification, rounded to whole dollars. Subject premium composition is the caller's responsibility -- this node does not compute manual premium from payrolls and rates and never vendors or reproduces NCCI or state rate tables. A mod of 0 or less flags and never yields a premium.

mod.description: NCCI experience modification factor; in a chain, art-346-compute-experience-mod's output_payload.mod read unchanged.

subject_premium.description: Total manual premium plus premium items subject to experience rating.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_modified_premium
mcp_tool_definition.description: Apply an NCCI experience modification factor to a caller-supplied subject premium (total manual premium plus premium items subject to experience rating) to get the modified premium, rounded to whole dollars. Subject premium composition is the caller's responsibility; manual premium is never computed from payrolls and rates, and no NCCI or state rate table is vendored.

source: authored from the pinned NCCI Basic Manual premium algorithm (ICRB Premium Algorithms) and the WCRB Wisconsin Basic Manual Whole Dollars - Premiums rounding rule; input_schema from the kernel's declared inputs
author: PostOakLabs

output_example.regulatory_basis: NCCI Basic Manual premium algorithm as published by the Indiana Compensation Rating Bureau (Premium Algorithms): add to manual premium all premium items subject to experience rating to get total subject premium, then apply the experience modification to arrive at the modified premium; premiums shown to the nearest dollar, a remainder of $0.50 or more rounded to the next higher dollar (WCRB Wisconsin Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Basic Manual, Whole Dollars - Premiums).
output_example.note: Subject premium composition is the caller's responsibility -- this kernel does not compute manual premium from payrolls and rates, and never vendors or reproduces NCCI or state rate tables. Out of scope: premium discount, expense constant, terrorism/catastrophe surcharges, state taxes, schedule rating and assigned-risk surcharge. The NCCI algorithm does not apply in the monopolistic state funds (Ohio, North Dakota, Washington, Wyoming) or the Puerto Rico and USVI funds.
